text: Sarah Young (March 15, 1946 – August 31, 2023) was an American author renowned for her contributions to Christian literature, particularly through her book *Jesus Calling*. She advocated for contemplative prayer and her books have sold over 45 million units worldwide, making her one of the most successful Christian authors in history. Born on March 15, 1946, in Nashville, Tennessee, Sarah Jane Kelly was the daughter of Douglass (Levine) Kelly and Tom Kelly, both educators. She graduated from E. C. Glass High School in Lynchburg, Virginia, earned a degree in philosophy from Wellesley College in 1968, and obtained a master's degree in child development from Tufts University in 1974. While in graduate school, a lapsed Christian, Young encountered the work of evangelical theologian Francis Schaeffer, whose influence significantly shaped her spiritual path. She visited L'Abri, an evangelical center in Switzerland, where she experienced a spiritual encounter and converted to Christianity. She then enrolled at Covenant Theological Seminary in Creve Coeur, Missouri, where she met her husband, Stephen Young, a third-generation missionary. They married in 1977 and served as Presbyterian missionaries near Yokkaichi, Japan for eight years, during which time Young gave birth to her two children. After Japan, the family moved to Atlanta, Georgia, where Young earned a master's degree in counseling from Georgia State University. In 1991, they relocated to Melbourne, Australia, where Young established a Christian counseling practice for women who had been sexually or spiritually abused. During meditation on God’s protection and visualization of loved ones surrounded by the Holy Spirit, she had a mystical experience in which she was enveloped by light and overwhelmed with peace. In 2001, the couple moved to Perth, where Young’s chronic health conditions—Lyme disease, melanoma, and vertigo—frequently left her housebound. In 2013, they moved to Nashville, Tennessee. Young died on August 31, 2023, from leukemia at her home in Brentwood, Tennessee, at the age of 77. Beginning in 1992, Young maintained a devotional journal in which she practiced "listening prayers," writing down what she believed God was saying to her rather than what she wanted to say. This journal eventually became the foundation of *Jesus Calling*, which was published in 2004. Initially rejected by publishers, Young abandoned publishing efforts in 2001, but her work later attracted the attention of an executive at Integrity (later part of Thomas Nelson), who offered her a contract. The book began modestly but gained widespread popularity after a renewed marketing campaign by Thomas Nelson, becoming a bestseller in Christian literature. The success of *Jesus Calling* led to the release of sequels, including *Jesus Always* and *Jesus Today*, as well as related products such as calendars, journals, children's editions, podcasts, an app, a magazine, and a television show, collectively selling over 45 million units as of August 2023. Critics, including Kathy Keller of Redeemer Presbyterian Church, Randy Alcorn of Eternal Perspective Ministries, and Tim Challies of Grace Fellowship Church, have condemned Young’s message, accusing her of blasphemy, occultic practices, paganism, panentheism, idolatry, misleading teachings, and pietism. Young was known for her intense privacy, avoiding public appearances and giving interviews only via email. She remained committed to her faith, family, and writing throughout her life. In 2009, she traveled to the United States for six months to receive treatment for Lyme disease but saw little improvement. She was survived by her husband Stephen Young, their two children Stephanie van der Westhuizen and Eric Young, her three siblings, and six grandchildren.
